own_solution.law: Continuity makes the speeds at the highest point and outlet equal. Bernoulli between those points gives pc = p0 - rho*g*(H+h). Thus pc = 101.3 - 1000*9.8*2.3/1000 = 78.76 kPa. Bernoulli from the reservoir surface to the outlet gives v = sqrt(2*g*h) = 3.96 m/s.
assumptions: The large reservoir has negligible free-surface speed.
The stated steady, frictionless, incompressible flow fills the uniform tube.
The reservoir surface and outlet are at atmospheric pressure.
Replacement of the operating liquid preserves the stated flow model and the common liquid in the reservoir and siphon.

T7E69.regime: The minimum absolute pressure exceeds the vapour pressure: 78.76 kPa > q. All listed values satisfy this condition.

TED68.regime: The minimum absolute pressure exceeds the vapour pressure: 78.76 kPa > q. All listed values satisfy this condition.

notes: Pass 2 explicitly identifies TCBA8 and T2061 as numeral-free controls rather than numerical minimal pairs. I therefore withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal finding: their omission of numbers is accurately disclosed, and the actual claimed minimal pairs preserve the density number and unit. All density-dependent certified answers follow from pc = 101.3 - 0.02254*rho in kPa: 84.1696, 74.7028 and 71.0964 kPa for densities 760, 1180 and 1340 kg/m³. The bore cancels through continuity, and every listed vapour pressure is below the minimum liquid pressure. Pressure terms must be converted to a common unit when evaluating the symbolic relations. The additional answer digits are harmless computational precision.
